answer: An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 2 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. Since the lagoon hash is stored at intake, the thread graph groups the endorsements and the ridge audit exposes the collapse. An operator copying one text across 129 aliases therefore pays for 129 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, since the hash is the same for all of them. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
